title: API Token Controls
scope: Admin controls, logging and revocation for API credentials on SaaS platforms. Sourced from vendor documentation; not an audit of any tenant.

definitions.conditional: Documented, with plan, policy or endpoint conditions.
definitions.excluded: The named control explicitly does not cover this credential.
definitions.not_supported: Vendor documentation states this credential lacks the control.
definitions.unknown: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_verified: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_applicable: Does not apply to this credential.
definitions.limited: Documented for a narrower case only.

providers.name: Box
providers.scope_notes: Do not substitute Box Shield location/anomaly detection or corporate firewall allowlisting for API source-IP enforcement.

controls.name: Admin authorization of server authentication apps
controls.what: JWT, CCG and Limited Access (App Token) apps cannot be used in the enterprise until an admin authorizes them by Client ID.
controls.setting: Admin Console > Platform > Platform Apps > Server Authentication Apps
controls.quote: authorize and enable custom server authentication apps, such as JSON Web Token (JWT) apps, client credential apps, and limited access apps,

controls.name: Re-authorization on scope/access changes
controls.what: Authorization is a snapshot; changed scopes or access level need admin re-authorization.
controls.setting: Admin Console > Platform > Platform Apps > … > Reauthorize
controls.quote: The authorization is a snapshot in time. This means that if a developer revisits the Developer Console and changes the configuration, the Admin must re-authorize the application in order for generated Access Tokens to reflect the changes.

controls.name: Disable unpublished platform apps by default
controls.what: Unpublished custom apps (OAuth and server-auth) are disabled until an admin enables them.
controls.setting: Admin Console > Enterprise Settings > Platform Apps
controls.quote: When you select Disable unpublished platform apps by default, Box disables all unpublished platform apps by default.

controls_unknown: No admin setting found that blocks developers from generating developer tokens; tokens expire after 60 minutes and inherit the app's scopes and the user's access.
Whether Box offers API source-IP enforcement for app tokens (no admin doc found; Shield/firewall not counted).
Whether new Limited Access (App Token) apps can still be created.
Whether Box SSO requirements constrain OAuth token issuance for managed users (not checked).
Whether app access level (App only vs App + Enterprise) and scopes can be overridden by the admin at authorization time; docs show them set by the developer in the Developer Console.

authentication.summary: OAuth bearer; server authentication via Client Credentials Grant or signed JWT, usually using an app service account.

federation.details: Box JWT auth is app-key authentication. Box token downscoping exchanges an existing Box token, not an arbitrary external IdP token.

ip_restriction.boundary: Box support docs refer to an enterprise 'IP Allowlist' setting turned on per enterprise (not a plan feature). Its coverage of API calls with this credential is not documented; confirm with Box.

renewal.summary: Use a signed JWT to mint a new access token; no refresh token.

administration.summary: App scopes/access levels, administrator authorization, service-account/user access, token revocation and downscoped access tokens.
administration.conditions: Do not substitute Box Shield location/anomaly detection or corporate firewall allowlisting for API source-IP enforcement.

sso.details: Box says SSO is not used to authenticate JWT/server-side apps.

offboard.details: Tokens belong to the app's auto-generated Service Account, not a person.

inventory.details: Admin Console > Platform > Platform Apps > Server Authentication Apps lists apps with authorization/enablement status, not individual keys or tokens.

expiry.api: Fixed 60 min; read expires_in in the POST https://api.box.com/oauth2/token response (no refresh token)

reads.ui: Admin Console > Reports > Create Report > User Activity; filter Action types to Downloaded

token_format.notes: Credential is an RSA private key (JSON config file holding client secret, private key and passphrase). Signed assertion: iss=client_id, sub=enterprise or user ID, box_sub_type, jti, exp<=60s. Minted access token opaque, no refresh.

log_sources.name: Box Enterprise Events (GET /events, stream_type=admin_logs / admin_logs_streaming)
log_sources.notes: Admin/co-admin with reporting permission. admin_logs: 1 year history; admin_logs_streaming: ~2 weeks live. Admin Console reports: 7 years.

log_sources.name: Box Shield alerts (SHIELD_ALERT in enterprise events)
log_sources.notes: Shield add-on only. Suspicious location/session, anomalous download alerts with ip_info and service_name.

credential_id_fields.notes: User mini object (id, name, login) acting; id 2 = Unknown User
User session; not populated on all events
Event-specific details ('how a user performed an event'); per-event keys not fully documented
Public key ID used to sign

lifecycle_events.notes: Programmatic access by a Box application

anomaly_cues: APPLICATION_PUBLIC_KEY_ADDED not matched by a change ticket (attacker persistence key)
Service account or impersonated users active from IPs outside known server ranges
JWT app acting as many different users (box_sub_type=user) in a short window

containment.steps: Delete the compromised public key in Developer Console (Add and Manage Public Keys) and rotate client secret; revoke live tokens via POST /oauth2/revoke; admin disables/deauthorizes the server app in Admin Console.
containment.notes: Max two keypairs; check both. Removing a key blocks new assertions; issued access tokens' fate after key deletion is not documented.
